cohort_bench.name: Cohort Bench
cohort_bench.description: Five shapes of data, three inductive biases, and the half of the family's own argument that none of its three members has ever photographed. A 0.96 x 0.96 m plate carries a 0.84 m square field of 120 points, and four corner posts stand exactly as tall as the tallest wall so the world box is 0.96 x 0.164 x 0.96 in all fifteen cells before any cut is computed. Three artifacts declare an axis called cohort and all three declare the SAME FIVE WORDS - blobs, block, rings, braid, skew - which is the only unanimous vocabulary of that size in the corpus. But in every one of them the axis changes the SCATTER ONLY: enhanced_kmeans's @identity promises a Voronoi tessellation and its update_voronoi_regions builds k flat translucent squares parked at the centroids, behind a show_voronoi_regions that ships false; random_forest_visualization draws no boundary at all and says so in its own header; svm_visualization builds its boundary as a PRIMITIVE_POINTS cloud inside a timer-driven finalize_training, and its margin_meshes array is declared, cleared and never once appended to - the maximum-margin artifact draws no margin. This bench builds the missing instrument: centroid runs k-means at k=4 and stands the real Voronoi up as walls, axis runs one CART at depth 5 and draws each node's cut across its own rectangle, margin searches 180 directions for fewest errors then widest gap and draws three parallel planes. Deterministic from seed 20260730 - the family's own constant, identical in all three members - keyed to the POPULATION, so block and skew draw the same lattice. No randf outside it, no noise, no _process, no Timer.
dev_themes: supervision as a thing you can see the absence of
interactions: walk the cohort axis at cut=centroid and watch the walls stay five and stay wrong: k-means never sees a label, so it partitions the ring into wedges, halves the braid left from right, and cuts the uniform field into four territories nobody asked for. It is right exactly once, at blobs, and that is a coincidence rather than a success

put block under all three cuts: eleven walls under axis to approximate one diagonal line, one wall under margin that gets it exactly right, and four invented territories under centroid. That triple is the argument in three tiles

stand at rings, cut=axis and look for the staircase the forest's own header promises. It is not there - four cuts make a clean box, because a box separates a disc of radius r from an annulus whose inner radius exceeds r times root two, and at the family's proportions it does

compare block and skew at cut=centroid and then at cut=axis: the first pair is one photograph to the byte, the second is two of the furthest-apart cells in the sheet. Same 120 positions, two labellings, and one method that cannot see the difference
look at the points themselves under centroid: every post is the same neutral height, the mean of the two class heights. That is not a styling choice, it is the data k-means is actually handed
cohort_bench.capacity: SEE that an inductive bias is a SHAPE - a Voronoi diagram, a staircase of axis-aligned boxes, one plane with a slab - and that a family can declare five adversary datasets, agree on all five words, and never once draw the thing the adversaries were supposed to defeat

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE STAGE IS THE FOOTPRINT AND IT IS DRAWN BEFORE EITHER AXIS IS CONSULTED: a 0.96 x 0.96 m plate 0.024 m thick, and four 0.030 m corner posts standing exactly WALL_H = 0.140 m tall at x, z = +-0.465. The posts are the reason the AABB is a constant. Without them the height of the box would be a fact about which cut was picked - centroid always draws walls, but a cut that drew none would leave a 0.086 m box against a 0.164 m one, the camera would move between cells, and every measured pair would carry a framing difference it did not earn. The FIGURE inside the stage moves a great deal: the drawn population spans 0.76 x 0.34 m at blobs, 0.85 x 0.85 m at block and skew, 0.75 x 0.75 m at rings and 0.84 x 0.33 m at braid, and the wall count runs from 1 (blobs under axis) to 11 (block under axis). The world box is 0.96 x 0.164 x 0.96 in every one of the fifteen cells regardless. layout=ladder stands all five cohorts in a row at 1.10 m pitch, about 5.5 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the STAGE and nothing else: the plate spans x and z at +-0.48, and the tallest things in any cell are the four corner posts and the cut walls, both topping out at PLATE_T + WALL_H = 0.164. Nothing the two axes draw can exceed that: the posts are 0.020 m square and at most 0.062 m tall, the margin planes are half wall height, and every wall and every point is clipped inside the 0.84 m field, which is 0.06 m inside the plate on every side.

dna.default: cohort=blobs, cut=centroid. blobs because TWO OF THE THREE MEMBERS SHIP IT - enhanced_kmeans.gd:45 and svm_visualization.gd:91 both declare `= "blobs"`, random_forest_visualization.gd:78 declares `= "block"` and calls it its own shipped look. 2 of 3, counted rather than assumed, and the same 2-1 that decides how many clusters blobs has (two, not kmeans's three) and what shape skew's minority is (a corner box, not two satellite groups). centroid because BOTH OTHER MEMBERS POINT AT ENHANCED_KMEANS in their own @identity relationships lines - the forest says `depends on enhanced_kmeans`, the svm says `contrasts enhanced_kmeans` - so k-means is the family's hub; and because it is the member carrying the deepest debt, the one whose @identity names a Voronoi tessellation under `emerges` and whose code has never drawn one. NOTE WHAT THE DEFAULT CELL COSTS: it is the agreement case under the label-blind cut, so it is the plainest tile in the sheet and the one cell where all three biases are nearly right. That would normally be a bad place to solve framing on, except that framing here is set by the stage and the stage is identical in all fifteen cells, so the camera distance is the same whichever cell is measured.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, where each word came from, and which cut each one defeats. THE FAMILY FIRST, and it is a census before it is an argument: three artifacts declare an axis called `cohort` and ALL THREE DECLARE THE SAME FIVE WORDS - blobs, block, rings, braid, skew. That is the only unanimous five-word vocabulary in the corpus, and it is not one scene wearing three names: enhanced_kmeans.tscn, random_forest_visualization.tscn and svm_visualization.tscn are three distinct scenes on three distinct scripts, checked. The declarations differ only in ORDER and DEFAULT: two list blobs first and ship it, the forest lists block first and ships that.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, and it is the finding. The brief said the five shapes are ADVERSARIES, each chosen to defeat a particular inductive bias. That is true of the DATA and false of the PICTURE. IN ALL THREE MEMBERS, `cohort` CHANGES ONLY THE SCATTER, AND NOT ONE OF THEM RELIABLY PHOTOGRAPHS WHAT ITS METHOD DOES TO IT.

  enhanced_kmeans - its @identity says the algorithm makes a `Voronoi tessellation of space`. Nothing in the file draws a Voronoi. update_voronoi_regions() builds ONE flat PlaneMesh per centroid, sized data_space_size/2 square, POSITIONED AT the centroid, at alpha 0.1: k stacked translucent squares, not a partition. And `show_voronoi_regions` ships FALSE, so it never renders at all. The centroids themselves move under _process at iteration_speed 1.5, so where they are when the shutter opens is a fact about the clock, which is exactly why that member REFUSED iteration_speed as an axis.

  random_forest_visualization - draws no decision boundary anywhere in 1226 lines. Its trees are node-and-edge diagrams on a Timer hanging BELOW the scatter, and its own header says so: the trees `may be absent or mid-grow when the shutter opens, so the axis is legible in the SCATTER ALONE`. The two volumes it does draw, at braid and skew, are the TRUE class regions, not the forest's cuts. `show_ensemble_prediction` is exported and read by nothing.

  svm_visualization - create_boundary_mesh() samples the decision function on a 50 x 50 grid over 8 m and emits PRIMITIVE_POINTS wherever |f| < 0.1: the boundary is a point cloud, and it is built only inside finalize_training(), at the end of a Timer-driven SMO loop at step_delay 0.1. `margin_meshes` is declared, cleared in clear_previous_visualization, and NEVER ONCE APPENDED TO. THE MAXIMUM-MARGIN ARTIFACT DRAWS NO MARGIN. `show_decision_boundary` and `show_margin_lines` are read by nothing either.

So the family built the battery and never built the instrument. This bench builds the instrument: the same five shapes, and the boundary as REAL GEOMETRY - walls standing in the field, computed synchronously from the points, with no clock anywhere.

COHORT, five values, the family's own five in the order two of three declare them. 120 points in every value, so no pair is separated by how much data there is.

  blobs - TWO DISCS, radius 0.17 m at x = +-0.21, 60 points each, AND THE LEFT DISC IS THE EXACT MIRROR OF THE RIGHT. The shape k-means was built for and the family's majority default. It defeats NOTHING, and that is its job: it is the agreement case, the one cell where all three biases are right, and it is the reference the other four fail against. The mirror is load-bearing rather than decorative - it makes the gap symmetric about x = 0, which puts the only zero-impurity axis-aligned split at exactly x = 0.000000 and makes the widest-gap direction exactly x-hat, so `axis` and `margin` draw the same wall to the micron. That is the pre-registered closest pair. THE FAMILY DISAGREES ABOUT THE COUNT: kmeans builds THREE gaussian discs plus 10 noise points (natural_cluster_count 3), the forest builds two 3.0 m balls 6.0 m apart on the cube diagonal, the svm builds two 4.0 x 5.0 m clouds 2.0 m apart in x. Two wins 2-1.

  block - A FILLED 12 x 10 LATTICE, 120 cells at 0.070 x 0.084 m pitch, each dot jittered 0.006 m inside its own cell, LABELLED FROM THE CELL CENTRE by x + z >= 0. That comes out at exactly 60 and 60 - counted on the replica, 1+2+3+4+5+7+8+9+10+11 over the ten rows. DEFEATS `axis`, and it is the only cohort that does: the true boundary is one straight line that is not axis-aligned, and the tree spends ELEVEN CUTS approximating it. It also defeats `centroid`, which invents four territories in a field that has no clusters. It is EASY for `margin` - zero errors at exactly 45 degrees - but the gap it finds is 0.004 m, which is svm_visualization's own caption for this value: `the thing being maximised has nowhere to sit`. A lattice rather than a uniform draw is that member's own repair and the reason is in `declines`.

  rings - 48 points in a 0.13 m core inside 72 on a 0.34 m shell 0.07 m thick. ALL THREE MEMBERS SPLIT THIS 40/60 INDEPENDENTLY - kmeans CORE_N 40 / RING_N 60, the forest 40 / 60, the svm 0.4 / 0.6 of the total - which is the strongest agreement anywhere in the family. DEFEATS `margin`: the best straight line over 180 directions gets 42 of 120 wrong against a do-nothing baseline of 48, so it beats doing nothing by six points. DEFEATS `centroid`: a Voronoi cell cannot express a shell, so the four sites quarter the ring like a pie. BUT IT DOES NOT DEFEAT `axis`, AND THE STAIRCASE THE FOREST'S OWN HEADER PROMISES HERE DOES NOT EXIST. That header says a boundary of axis-aligned cuts `has to approximate a sphere, and the staircase it produces is the argument this artifact should be able to make`. The arithmetic says otherwise: a box separates a disc of radius r from an annulus exactly whenever the annulus's inner radius exceeds r x sqrt(2), because sqrt(2) r is where the box's corner reaches, and at the family's own proportions - core 0.35 of the outer edge - it does. 0.13 x 1.414 = 0.184 against an inner radius of 0.305. FOUR CUTS, A CLEAN BOX, NO STAIRCASE. The forest's numbers have the same property (core 0.75 m, shell inner 2.6 m), so the claim is overstated in the source too.

  braid - two sinusoidal bands, amplitude 0.13 m, period 0.42 m, 0.05 m apart, 60 points each, x stratified so the bands read as bands. THE NEAREST THING TO A UNIVERSAL ADVERSARY. Defeats `margin` hardest - 41 of 120 wrong where chance is 60, so it is barely better than a coin. Defeats `centroid`, which halves the field left from right and cuts both bands in two. And it is the only cohort where `axis` gets an answer that is an APPROXIMATION rather than a solution: eight axis-aligned cuts spent tracing two smooth curves, and eight is where the depth ceiling stops it, not where the data does. IT IS ALSO THE ONE VALUE WHERE ALL THREE MEMBERS BUILD A DIFFERENT SHAPE: kmeans makes two Archimedean spiral arms phase-offset by PI, the forest makes eight alternating axis-aligned slabs, the svm makes two offset sine bands. One word, three geometries - the only outright disagreement in the vocabulary, and it lands on the value that is hardest for everything. The svm's reading is used here and the reason is in `declines`.

  skew - THE SAME 120 LATTICE POSITIONS AS `block`, relabelled 114 / 6 with the six minority points in a BOX at the +x +z corner (columns 9-11 by rows 8-9). The forest's and the svm's ratio, 95/5, on this bench's 120 points; kmeans instead builds 88 plus two 6-point groups at 11 m, so 2-1 again. DEFEATS `centroid` and nothing else: k-means splits the majority mass into four territories and the pocket is not even a rounding error to it. `axis` handles it natively in TWO cuts, because the pocket is a box and a box is what an axis-aligned method is made of. `margin` gets 1 of 120 wrong. THE FAILURE THIS VALUE ACTUALLY NAMES IS NOT PHOTOGRAPHABLE and that is written down rather than hidden: the forest's own claim is that a five-tree MAJORITY VOTE reaches 95 percent by never predicting the minority, which is an ENSEMBLE effect of bootstrap resampling at 0.8 plus voting. One unpruned tree finds the pocket easily. The cost of ignoring it is a number, not a picture.

SO WHERE IS THE COHORT THAT DEFEATS ALL THREE? THERE ISN'T ONE, and the brief asked for it. Measured: rings and skew fall cleanly to `axis`, block falls exactly to `margin`, blobs falls to everything. The only method defeated by all five is `centroid`, and it is defeated for the same reason every time - it never sees a label, so it can only be right by coincidence, and blobs is that coincidence. The battery is a COVERING SET, not a killer: each shape defeats at least one bias and is handled by at least one other, which is a better fact than the one the brief wanted, because it is what makes the three methods worth having side by side.

CUT, three values, one per member, and every hyperparameter is the member's own rather than this bench's.

  centroid - enhanced_kmeans. k-means at k = 4, which is that member's `cluster_count: int = 4`, k-means++ initialised from the same seeded generator, Lloyd to a fixed point or 40 iterations, an empty cluster keeping its site. Then the ACTUAL VORONOI: each site's cell is the field square clipped by one half-plane per rival, which is the definition of the cell and not an approximation of it, and every interior bisector is stood up as a wall. Five interior walls at every cohort. THE POINTS ARE DRAWN UNLABELLED HERE - one neutral post each, at POST_U 0.044 m, the arithmetic mean of the two class heights, in C_UNLAB, whose Rec.709 luminance 0.610 is the mean of the two class luminances to within 0.003. That is not styling. K-MEANS IS UNSUPERVISED AND THAT IS THE DATA IT IS HANDED, and the whole designed null follows from it.

  axis - random_forest_visualization. One CART, Gini, splits at the midpoints of consecutive distinct values, max depth 5 and min_samples_split 2 from that member's own `max_depth: int = 5` and `min_samples_split: int = 2`. EACH INTERNAL NODE'S CUT IS A WALL SPANNING ONLY ITS OWN RECTANGLE, which is what turns the recursion into a staircase instead of a set of full-width lines - and it is why the wall count is legible as an answer: 1 at blobs, 2 at skew, 4 at rings, 8 at braid, 11 at block. Supervised.

  margin - svm_visualization, LINEAR branch. One separator chosen by exhaustive search over 180 directions at one degree, FEWEST ERRORS FIRST AND THEN WIDEST GAP - and the second half of that rule is the only place the word margin earns its keep, because without it this is an accuracy method and not a margin method. Drawn as three parallel walls: the decision plane at full height and full thickness, and the two margin planes at half height and two thirds thickness, because they mark the gap rather than the decision. Three walls at every cohort, whatever the data - which is the brief's own observation about linear methods, kept. Supervised.

HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP, and it matters more here than usual because class colour is the first thing a machine-learning visualisation reaches for - all three members do it, in green and red. The critic measures luminance by default and has a separate per-channel rescue, so a pair separated only by hue at constant brightness reads as a twin in greyscale. CLASS IS THEREFORE CARRIED IN TWO CHANNELS AT ONCE: height, 0.026 m against 0.062 m, and albedo, Rec.709 0.785 against 0.428. Neither channel alone is relied on anywhere. The full luminance ladder is plate 0.180, corner post 0.309, class 1 0.428, margin plane 0.561, unlabelled 0.610, class 0 0.785, wall 0.899 - no two things that must be told apart sit within 0.10 of each other. If the colour-only rescue ever fires on this sheet it is reporting a fault, not a rescue.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: an inductive bias is a SHAPE, and a family that names five adversary datasets without ever drawing the shapes has published the question and withheld the answer. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: a reader can say the members are teaching artifacts about ALGORITHMS, that an algorithm is a process and a still cannot hold one, and that drawing a frozen boundary substitutes a picture for the thing. The answer is that all three already promise the boundary - one in its @identity, one in an export it never reads, one in an array it never fills - and that a promise made in three files and kept in none is a gap rather than a genre. The cell where holding the thesis costs something is skew under margin, where the honest instrument reports 1 error out of 120 and the failure the value is named for turns out to be an ensemble effect that no still can show.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: cut=axis against cut=margin, in the blobs cohort
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
THE CONTEXT IS THE `blobs` COLUMN AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT: three pairs, axis-margin 26.0, centroid-axis about 62, centroid-margin about 64. The two centroid pairs are far because that cut redraws all 120 posts (unlabelled 0.044 m at luminance 0.610, against 0.026/0.062 m at 0.785/0.428) as well as swapping 5 Voronoi walls for 1; the named pair changes nothing but two objects.

WHY THAT PAIR IS THE FLOOR OF THE SHEET, AND IT IS BY CONSTRUCTION. `blobs` is built as 60 points in the right disc and their EXACT MIRROR on the left. The mirror makes the empty gap symmetric about x = 0, so (a) the only zero-impurity axis-aligned split is the single candidate lying in that gap, whose midpoint is x = 0.000000 exactly, and both children are pure so the tree stops after ONE cut; and (b) the widest-gap direction is exactly x-hat, which the 180-direction search reaches at theta = 0, with b = 0.000000 and zero errors. Verified on the replica: axis walls = 1 at x = 0.000000; margin theta = 0.0 deg, b = +0.0000, errors 0. SO THE DECISION WALL AND THE TREE'S ONLY WALL ARE THE SAME OBJECT, same position, same 0.009 m thickness, same 0.140 m height, and the 120 posts are identical vertex for vertex. THE ENTIRE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO FRAMES IS TWO MARGIN PLANES.

THE NUMBER. Replica gap 0.1206 m, so the planes sit at x = +-0.0603, each 0.84 m long in z, 0.070 m tall, 0.006 m thick. Camera is capture_config_sweep's: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, framing 0.60 on the union AABB - which is the STAGE at 0.96 x 0.164 x 0.96, diagonal 1.3675 m, so the frame is 1.3675 x 1.9 x 0.60 = 1.559 m across in every cell. Screen basis at that standpoint: x-hat -> (0.8139, 0.1494), z-hat -> (0.5810, 0.2093), y-hat -> (0, 0.9664). One plane projects to a parallelogram of 0.84 x (0.5810, 0.2093) against 0.070 x (0, 0.9664) = 0.0330 m2, plus 0.0013 for its lit top face = 0.0343 m2. The two are 0.1206 m apart in x, which is a screen offset of (0.0982, 0.0180); its component perpendicular to the parallelogram's long axis is 0.0164 against a perpendicular thickness of 0.0636, so they overlap 74 percent and the union is 0.0343 x 1.258 = 0.0431 m2.

The subject box is the plate plus the corner posts: 0.96 x (0.8139 + 0.5810) = 1.339 m wide by 0.96 x (0.1494 + 0.2093) + 0.164 x 0.9664 = 0.503 m tall = 0.6735 m2. So the changed area is 6.40 percent of the subject box. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes - identical here, because the stage is - neutralises each frame's own corner, greys, resizes to 160 x 160 = 25600 px, and takes the mean of the hottest 5 percent = 1280 px. 6.40 percent of 25600 is 1639 changed pixels, MORE than the 1280-pixel window, so THE WINDOW FILLS ENTIRELY WITH MARGIN-PLANE PIXELS AND THE NUMBER IS SET BY CONTRAST, NOT BY AREA. The planes stand in the empty gap between the two discs, so about 80 percent of that silhouette is against C_PLATE and 20 percent against posts: |0.561 - 0.180| = 97 of 255 for the plate, about 45 of 255 for the posts, weighted 86.6 of 255 = 34.0 percent of albedo separation. Applying the lighting-and-tonemap compression the substance_room replica measured at 0.77 gives 26.2. Registered at 26.0.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. The replica has one key, flat shading, no shadows, no AO, no antialiasing, and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 26.0 ON THE NAMED PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py, because a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles; (b) _rejects.json, because all three exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=15, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 5 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `cut` collapses to [centroid] alone, which deletes both supervised cuts, the designed null's contrast case and the entire prediction.

THE ONE QUANTITY HERE THAT IS GENERATOR-DEPENDENT is the gap. 0.1206 m is the Python replica's draw; Godot's PCG32 will produce a different one, expected between 0.09 and 0.14 for 60 uniform-in-disc samples, which moves the two planes by at most 0.010 m each and changes the overlap fraction rather than the contrast. Since the window fills either way, the predicted percent is insensitive to it. NOTHING ELSE IN THIS PREDICTION DEPENDS ON A DRAW: the wall at x = 0.000000 and the zero errors are consequences of the mirror and hold for any seed.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS THE THESIS, not a spare check. `block` and `skew` are ONE POPULATION UNDER TWO LABELLINGS - the same 12 x 10 lattice, the same jitter draws in the same order out of a generator seeded from the POPULATION index rather than the cohort index, verified position-for-position on the replica. They agree on 66 of the 120 labels and disagree on 54. `centroid` is k-means, which never reads a label: _kmeans_sites() does not touch _lab, and under this cut the points are drawn UNLABELLED, one neutral post each at the mean of the two class heights, because that is the data k-means is handed. So the two frames are the same 120 posts, the same four converged sites, the same five Voronoi walls, and the same stage. THIS IS NOT INVENTED FOR THE BENCH: in random_forest_visualization, _gen_block and _gen_skew are BOTH uniform fills of the same 8 m cube and differ only in how labels are assigned, and in svm_visualization the two values were once literally the same 95 positions out of the same seeded generator - a bug that member repaired by making block a lattice, and recorded in its own header. Predicted 0.00 percent focus and 0.00 percent frame. Anything above 0.5 percent is render noise; anything above 2 percent means the centroid rig is reading a label it must not, or the population seed is keyed to the cohort after all, and nothing else in the sheet can be believed until it is found. THE CONTRAST THAT MUST HOLD ALONGSIDE IT: the same two cohorts under `axis` and under `margin` should be among the widest pairs in the sheet, because 54 of 120 posts change both height and albedo. A null that held under all three cuts would mean the supervised cuts are not reading labels either.

dna.designed_nulls_why: ONE NULL, ONE FACT, AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A CHECK ON IT. Only one pair in this sheet is identical by construction, and it says the thing the bench exists to say: the same 120 points are an easy problem and an impossible one depending on a labelling that one of the three methods is constitutionally unable to see. Every other pair differs in the point cloud, because `cohort` is the population and the population is always drawn - which is why the brief's suggested null (a linear cut being one plane whatever the data, so several cohorts give the same picture) is NOT constructible here and is recorded as declined rather than quietly dropped: `margin` does draw exactly three parallel walls at all five cohorts, but their angle and offset are fitted, and the body underneath them is never the same twice. The tempting second null is blobs under axis against blobs under margin, where the tree's only wall and the decision plane ARE the same object to the micron - and it is deliberately NOT a null, because two margin planes remain and that 26.0 percent is the pre-registered closest pair.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all five cohorts in a row (layout=ladder, 1.10 m pitch, about 5.5 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a five-wide row in the same spec would frame every single cell against five and a half metres and photograph the 0.009 m walls as hairs. layout is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no unseeded draw here. Every point comes from one RandomNumberGenerator seeded from DATA_SEED 20260730 - the family's own constant, written independently and identically in all three members - offset by the POPULATION index; the four k-means initialisations come from the same seed plus 7717; there is no _process, no Timer, no tween, no FastNoiseLite and deliberately no NoiseTexture2D, which bakes on a worker thread and would let the shutter catch an unbaked map. That matters because the sources are the opposite of quiet: enhanced_kmeans moves its centroids every frame under _process and its own convergence state decides what a still shows, random_forest_visualization grows its trees on a Timer at training_speed 0.5, and svm_visualization builds its entire boundary at the end of a timer-driven SMO loop. All three refused their time-domain exports as axes for exactly this reason; this bench has no time-domain exports to refuse.
dna.kin: The three sources are the kin, and the relation is unusually direct because this bench shares their word and their five values rather than inventing any. enhanced_kmeans is a 50 m field of drifting pucks whose truth line is that clustering does not discover structure in data but imposes it by choosing K - and `centroid` here is that sentence drawn, because at k = 4 on a uniform lattice the four territories are entirely imposed. random_forest_visualization is a 20 m stand of trees whose truth line is that a forest of imperfect decision-makers can beat any single expert - and `axis` here is deliberately ONE tree, not a forest, which is declared and is why skew comes out easier here than that member's own header says. svm_visualization is a 10 m sheet whose truth line is that the boundary depends on only a few points, most of the data being redundant once the margin is found - and `margin` here is the only cut that draws the margin at all, which is the member's own missing half. A room holding this bench beside any one of the three is saying the same sentence twice about the data and for the first time about the method; a room holding it beside all three is the comparison the three of them describe in their `relationships` lines and cannot perform, because each one draws its own scatter at its own scale in its own scene. ON THE VALUE SIDE this is the corpus's cleanest shared vocabulary: five words, three members, three separate scenes, no disagreement about the list and only one disagreement about the geometry - `braid`.
declines: THE BRIEF'S ARGUMENT, corrected from the code, and it is the biggest change. The brief said the five shapes are adversaries each chosen to defeat a particular inductive bias, and that the family is testing three biases against one battery. THE BATTERY IS REAL AND THE TEST HAS NEVER BEEN RUN, because no member draws its bias. kmeans's Voronoi is k flat squares parked at the centroids behind a flag that ships false; the forest draws no boundary at all and says so in its own header; the svm's boundary is a point cloud built at the end of a Timer and its margin_meshes array is never appended to. So the bench's subject is not the five shapes - it is the missing instrument, and the five shapes are what the instrument is pointed at.

THE BRIEF'S CLAIM ABOUT THE LINEAR SVM, answered against the guess. It said a linear SVM cannot separate rings or braid without a kernel. svm_visualization SHIPS THE KERNEL: `kernel_type: String = "rbf"`, gamma 1.0, C 1.0, and its own DNA header calls rings `the honest advertisement for the kernel trick ... separable by the rbf kernel this artifact defaults to`. The linear case is one of four branches in kernel_function and is never the default. This bench draws the LINEAR cut anyway, and the reason is that a kernel is a claim about the FEATURE MAP, not about the cut: the tree's cuts and the centroid bisectors are both linear in the same two features, and swapping one of the three onto a different feature space would make every difference in the sheet a fact about the map rather than about the bias. So `margin`'s 42-of-120 failure at rings is a fact about the linear branch and is labelled as such wherever it appears. An rbf cut is the honest fourth value of this axis and the first thing to add if it ever needs one.

THE BRIEF'S REQUEST FOR A COHORT THAT DEFEATS ALL THREE. Measured on the replica, THERE ISN'T ONE. rings falls to `axis` in four cuts, skew in two, block falls to `margin` exactly, blobs falls to everything. The only method defeated by all five is `centroid`, for the same reason every time. `braid` is the nearest thing - wedged by centroid, 41 of 120 wrong under margin, and eight cuts spent approximating two curves - and it is registered as the nearest thing rather than promoted to the thing.

THE STAIRCASE AT `rings`, which random_forest_visualization's own header promises and the arithmetic refuses. A box separates a disc of radius r from an annulus exactly whenever the annulus's inner radius exceeds r x sqrt(2), and at the family's own proportions it does - 0.184 against 0.305 here, and 1.06 m against 2.6 m in that member's own numbers. Building rings tight enough to force a staircase would have meant a core at 0.59 of the outer edge instead of the family's 0.35, so the value would no longer be the family's value. The proportions were kept and the finding was written down instead. The real staircase is at `block` and it is eleven cuts long.

`skew`'S MINORITY AS A RANKING. The first build defined it as the six cells with the largest x + z, and THE REPLICA CAUGHT IT BEFORE ANY CAPTURE: a set defined that way is a half-plane by construction, so the margin cut came back with ZERO errors and the sheet would have published a failure case that the method solves perfectly. Both members that build a pocket build a BOX - random_forest_visualization's SKEW_CORNER 1.5 m cube, svm_visualization's SKEW_POCKET 0.9 m square - and a box is not linearly separable from an L-shaped complement. The code follows the members; the errors went from 0 to 1 and the axis-cut walls from 6 to 2.

A FOREST, rather than one tree, under `axis`. The characteristic skew failure the forest's header describes - a five-tree majority vote reaching 95 percent by never once predicting the minority - is an ENSEMBLE effect of bootstrap resampling at 0.8 plus voting, and one unpruned CART finds the pocket in two cuts. Drawing five bootstrapped trees' averaged decision regions was the alternative and was declined: the vote's boundary is a fractional field rather than a partition, so it would have to be drawn as a translucent volume, which is the one thing the forest member ALREADY does (its braid slabs and skew corner) and which draws the TRUE regions rather than the method's. One tree draws a partition, and a partition is a body.

`braid` AS SPIRAL ARMS OR AS SLABS. The three members build three different shapes under this one word and only one could be built. The svm's sine bands were taken because they are the only one of the three that is a genuine adversary to all three biases at once: kmeans's Archimedean arms are two clusters at every radius and a Voronoi does poorly but a tree does too, while the forest's eight axis-aligned slabs are TRIVIAL for an axis-aligned method by construction - the value is named for defeating the tree and is built out of exactly what the tree cuts with. That the family cannot agree on the shape of its hardest word is the finding; picking the svm's is the decline.

k = 2 FOR `centroid`, which would have bought a second designed null and was refused. With k equal to the number of classes and blobs built as a mirror pair, all three cuts land on x = 0.000000 and centroid-against-axis is a second exact null. But k = 2 is not any member's number - enhanced_kmeans ships `cluster_count: int = 4` - and it would also make nearest-centroid a linear classifier, collapsing two of the three cuts into the same KIND of object and making the sheet's differences a fact about how many regions each method was allowed. Every hyperparameter here is the member's own: k = 4, depth 5, min_samples_split 2. One null was worth less than that.

A DECISION-REGION FILL rather than walls. Colouring each region by its predicted class would read faster and would be a gauge: the eye would compare two colour maps instead of two bodies, and the wall count - 1 against 11 against 4 - is exactly the quantity that makes an inductive bias legible as a shape. It would also put class colour back at the centre of a sheet that is deliberately built so no pair is separated by hue alone.

ANIMATION, and every rate, duration and phase. All three members refused their time-domain exports as axes and all three still ship them: iteration_speed and animate_clustering, training_speed and animate_tree_growth, step_delay and show_optimization_steps. This bench has none to refuse - the whole figure is built synchronously inside _ready from arithmetic on one seeded generator - and that is not a stylistic preference but the reason the boundary can be photographed at all. A boundary that exists only after a Timer has fired is a boundary a still cannot report.

THE MEMBERS' SCALE. enhanced_kmeans is a 50 m field, the forest a 20 m stand, the svm a 10 m sheet, and their `cohort` numbers are in those metres. Everything here is rebuilt at 0.84 m of field with the RATIOS preserved and the ratios named in the note - 40/60 at rings, 95/5 at skew, 2 percent jitter at braid, one lattice pitch at block - so the arithmetic is checkable against the sources even though not one absolute number is shared with them. The exception is the seed, which is 20260730 in all four files.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=15 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. `cohort` is declared first and is never trimmed; `cut` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 5 x 3 sheet renders as 5 x 1 = `centroid` only, which deletes both supervised cuts, the pre-registered pair, and the contrast case that makes the designed null mean anything - and leaves a finished-looking sheet of five unlabelled scatters with five Voronoi walls each that cannot be wrong about anything. At --max=12 it renders 5 x 2 = centroid and axis, which keeps the null and its contrast and deletes the prediction. Only 15 carries the experiment.
